From the owner
It is one of the first questions we get once new countertops go in, and the honest answer depends entirely on the material. Granite is porous, so it needs periodic resealing, generally every one to five years depending on the stone's color and density. A simple water test tells you when it's due: if a few drops bead up on the surface, the seal is holding; if they darken or soak in, it's time to reseal. Engineered quartz, on the other hand, does not require sealing at all, which is one reason it has become such a popular low-maintenance choice. Knowing which rule applies to your countertop saves an unnecessary chore, or an overdue one.

Meet Josh, bringing 16 years of residential, commercial, and civil construction experience to the Flint Contracting team. How to Personalize Your Home: Easy Interior Updates That Reflect You The most inviting homes aren’t necessarily the most expensive or on-trend. They’re the ones that reflect the people who live there. Personalizing your space doesn’t require a full remodel or a large budget. A few thoughtful updates can make any room feel authentic and uniquely yours. Start by displaying what you love. Travel souvenirs, family heirlooms, meaningful artwork, favorite books, and collected pieces tell your story. A gallery wall or styled shelf can add warmth and personality. Color is a powerful way to transform a room. Whether you prefer a bold accent wall, soft earthy tones, or a cheerful pop of color, choose shades you’re naturally drawn to rather than following trends. Layering textures makes a space feel finished and welcoming. Mix linen, leather, wool, velvet, and natural wood through rugs, pillows, throws, and furnishings. Don’t overlook lighting. Replacing builder-grade fixtures with something sculptural, vintage, playful, or refined can change a room. Think of lighting as jewelry for your home. Finally, incorporate one-of-a-kind pieces. A vintage mirror, handmade table, custom artwork, or reupholstered family chair adds character that can’t be replicated. Above all, decorate for yourself, not for a magazine. Your home should grow and evolve with you, telling your story one meaningful piece at a time. Start with one small update and watch how quickly your space feels more like home

From the owner
We have all seen it. A brown or yellowish stain spreading across a ceiling. If that spot appears in your home, it is time to act. At Palm Restore, the reason we do what we do is simple: to take care of you. One of the most common issues we find is water damage that was left unaddressed for too long. People often wait, hoping the stain will dry out or stop growing on its own. That ceiling spot indicates hidden moisture is at play. It may be a sign of a roof leak or plumbing issue and while the stain itself may be small, the problem behind it may not be. Damp and moldy environments can really wreck havoc on our health. We've seen it cause symptoms including a stuffy nose, sore throat, coughing, wheezing, eye irritation, and skin irritation. People with asthma, mold allergies, chronic lung conditions, or weakened immune systems may be especially vulnerable. The EPA advises drying water-damaged areas within 24 to 48 hours when possible and fixing the water source quickly to help prevent mold growth. Do not wait for the stain to get bigger or for the musty smell to become harder to ignore. Call Palm so we can provide professional water damage restoration, moisture detection, and drying services for your home or business.

From the owner
Replacing your kitchen cabinets? Here is what usually stays, what goes, and what it costs in a San Antonio home. What usually stays: your walls, the sink under the window, the range on its gas line, the outlets and, most of the time, your appliances. A same-footprint swap usually needs no permit. What usually goes: the old cabinets and the countertops. Stone tops are glued to the old boxes and can crack when they are lifted, so plan on new tops, templated once the new cabinets are set and level. Check your floor, too. In many homes the tile stops at the toe kick, so moving a cabinet can leave a gap. What it costs: for a standard 10x10 kitchen, cabinets only start at $1,750. A turn-key kitchen with countertops, hardware, delivery and installation by our own crew starts at $5,500. With counters and labor, most 10x10 replacements land between $5,000 and $10,000. How long: about 2 to 6 weeks to build after you approve your design, then 1 to 2 days to install the cabinets. Approve your design by about October 20, and Christmas in a finished kitchen is realistic even at the long end of the build. It starts with a free in-home measurement: 60 to 90 minutes, no trip charge. You get a 3D design and an itemized quote within 48 hours. Our Isom Rd showroom is open 7 days, and walk-ins are welcome. Se habla español. Pictured: white Shaker wall cabinets over wood-tone base cabinets, from our project gallery. Tap Learn more to read the full replacement guide.
